bug_semantics: Cross-tenant payroll IDOR/missing authorization on two authenticated paths: the GET/POST /payroll listing starts from Payroll::where('period_year', $year) and, when no user_id filter is supplied, returns every company's payroll rows, while POST /payroll/save accepts any globally existing user.id and persists it as payroll.user_id. A caller with payroll privileges can therefore read another tenant's employee name, gross/net salary, IBAN, file, and notes, or create a payroll record attributed to another tenant's employee.
flaw_origin: The smallest exploitable BIC is PR #258 member 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6, not its squash 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64 and not the 2024 WIP skeleton 5804831d829fd5cb275ba7aef1962a960511a415. The older skeleton had a latent unscoped getAllByYear query, but its payroll table body rendered no records, PayrollSaveController::save was a no-op, and PayrollRequest did not exist. Commit 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 simultaneously made the disclosure and creation paths operative: it added the unscoped period_year listing and rendered sensitive fields, created the global exists:user,id rule, and persisted that validated foreign key.

reasoning: The vulnerability requires an authorization failure and an observable/useful sink. Commit 5804831d829fd5cb275ba7aef1962a960511a415 created a latent company-unscoped payroll helper, but the direct pre-BIC tree still rendered no payroll records and could not save one; treating that WIP as the BIC would confuse an antecedent query with the described exploitable lifecycle. PR #258's direct member 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 is the smallest commit that joins attacker-reachable payroll keys to both sinks: no-filter listing results are rendered with sensitive tenant data, and any globally existing employee ID is accepted and persisted. Its parent 9e4f84ece7e13c2c327540804dcaf841c6ac23fa lacks those exact lines and behaviors. The member was squashed with a route-only follow-up as 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64, so the member—not the aggregate—is the BIC. Later 5cc01ed958db4ad0a026a8daa1c6a8bb98a43e66 placed a company filter only inside the optional employee filter and therefore left the no-filter disclosure intact. Direct fix fdfd7dd3a5747c3392c66e3240be3ccf31181776 closes both paths; final squash 59644f910b7d1aec7d1ac962b0354b3ec209977e lands the fixed tree and 5.15.10 boundary. Because the exact BIC commit object has human author/committer identities and no AI marker, the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
